newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police fire in air to disperse protesters.
newsitem.headline: Indian police fire in air to disperse protesters.

text.p: Indian police fired in the air to disperse hundreds of people protesting on Monday against the killing of six people by rebels supporting Indian control over troubled Kashmir, police said.
They said no one was injured in the demonstration in the town of Pulwama, 35 kilometres (22 miles) south of Srinagar, the summer capital of the Himalayan state of Jammu and Kashmir.
The guerrillas killed six people on Sunday night in the village of Ratnipora near Pulwama, police said.

"Militants of Ikhwan-ul-Muslimoon raided Ratnipora village last night and crashed into several houses, dragged many people out of their homes and shot them dead," Pulwama resident Hassina Akhtar told Reuters by telephone.
More than a dozen militant groups in Kashmir are fighting for either independence or merger with Pakistan. India controls two-thirds of Kashmir and Pakistan the rest.
The Ikhwan-ul-Muslimoon is a group of former separatist rebels that now supports Indian control over the region.
Witnesses said the protesters hurled stones at police, shouting anti-India and anti-Ikhwan slogans.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in Kashmir since a separatist rebellion began seven years ago.
